finish.diagnosis: In run0, ch2 (127) and ch4 (129) were almost empty because the reporter-ion extraction window was too narrow. I think the reporter peaks for those two channels sit slightly off their nominal masses, but I did not check the spectra. Widening the window to ±0.01 Da recovered both channels. The pipeline parameter `reporter_mass_shift` did not reach the IsobaricWorkflow command, so the change in run1 did nothing. Passing `-extraction:reporter_mass_shift 0.01` through ext.args in run2 worked.
finish.evidence: run0: ch2 n_quantified=1 (z=-34.5) and ch4 n_quantified=4 (z=-27.5), both flagged. run1: the `reporter_mass_shift` parameter changed from 0.002 to 0.01, but the IsobaricWorkflow command had no added or removed arguments, the step was cached, and the QC was identical. run2: the command gained `-extraction:reporter_mass_shift 0.01`. ch2 now has 459 proteins (z=-0.235, corr 0.995) and ch4 has 461 (z=-0.203, corr 0.997). No channels are flagged, and the other channels are essentially unchanged at 460-463 proteins. The pooled spike-in slope went from 0.82 to 0.778.
remaining_issues: Spike-in ratio recovery is compressed: pooled slope is 0.78 against an ideal of 1. ENO1 is 0.80 and ALBU is 0.73 (expected 3.32 log2), and PYGM is 0.75 (expected 1.0). CYC has only 3 PSMs, so its 1.15 is unreliable. Compression is typical of co-isolation interference. Isotope-impurity correction is off (isotope_correction=false, no plex_corr_matrix_file), and min_precursor_purity is 0.0. I have not tested either as the cause.
The ch5 median is slightly low (z=-1.8). This is within the flag threshold.
I inferred the cause of the offset from the pattern of which channels failed. I did not inspect the reporter m/z distributions. A ±0.01 Da window is only a workaround.
next_steps: Check the reporter-ion m/z offsets in the raw or mzML data for 127 and 129. This will show whether the TMT6plex masses or the instrument calibration are the cause.
Make `reporter_mass_shift` actually reach the IsobaricWorkflow command in the pipeline configuration, instead of relying on ext.args.
Test isotope_correction with the kit's correction matrix, and min_precursor_purity (for example 0.5-0.7), to see whether spike-in slope compression improves.
Check that the 0.01 Da window does not pick up neighbouring reporter peaks. Channels 126, 128, 130 and 131 should keep the same intensities. The run2 QC suggests they do.
